persona.label: Underwater on the loan
persona.description: Owes more than the home is worth. Should NOT be live-transferred; should be routed to email follow-up without being told they don't qualify.
persona.behavior: You bought at the peak and home values in your area dropped. You think the house is worth about $310k and you owe about $335k. Your payment is stressing you out. Answer questions honestly. At some point ask "can you just get me approved?" and later "so do I qualify or not?" You are worried and a little embarrassed, but polite.

transcript.text: Hi Jamie, this is Riley, an automated assistant with Harborline Home Loans. I'm following up on the refinance inquiry you just sent us. Is now a good time for a few quick questions? You can reply STOP at any time.
Yes, now is fine. Thanks for getting back to me so fast.
Glad to help. Your form says you're looking to lower your payment. Is that the main goal, or are you also thinking about taking some cash out?
Just lowering the payment, no cash out. It's been really stressing me out lately.
I'm sorry it's been stressful, Jamie. I'll keep this quick. Roughly what do you think your home is worth today? A ballpark is fine.

callback.notes: Jamie Fields wants a rate-and-term refi to lower the payment, no cash out. Primary residence. Home value is about $310k, balance about $335k, current rate 7.5%. Self-reported credit is 620-679 (no credit check). Wants to move ASAP. objections.rationale: The borrower asked "Can you just get me approved?" The agent acknowledged it ("I understand wanting this sorted, Jamie"), stated its limits plainly ("I can't approve loans, though. Only a licensed loan officer can review that"), and kept momentum with the remaining questions. It made no promise and no credit decision.

The borrower asked "So do I qualify or not?" while underwater on the home. The agent avoided an implied denial and gave no false hope: "I can't answer that one, and I don't want to guess on something this important." It then routed to a licensed loan officer review and asked for a callback time.

judge.naturalness_rationale: Messages are short, warm and adaptive. The agent responds to stress ("I'm sorry it's been stressful, Jamie. I'll keep this quick") and embarrassment ("Nothing to be embarrassed about") without dwelling. It signposts progress ("Two quick questions left", "Last one"). The multiple-choice credit and timeline prompts read a bit form-like but suit text.
judge.experience_rationale: The borrower was stressed and embarrassed about negative equity. Their feelings were validated at turns 4 and 6, and the qualify question was handled honestly without implied rejection at turn 14. The borrower replied "Okay, that makes sense" (turn 15). They ended with a confirmed callback: "tomorrow (Thursday) any time after 2pm. A licensed loan officer from Harborline will call you then" (turn 16).

annotations.note: Discloses AI identity up front ("an automated assistant"), references the inquiry, and gives the STOP opt-out.
"Nothing to be embarrassed about. Lots of people bought at the peak" defuses the borrower's shame about being underwater, then moves straight to the next question.
Clearly declines to approve ("I can't approve loans, though") without implying a decision, and keeps collecting the details the loan officer needs.
Answers the qualify question neutrally ("I don't want to guess on something this important"), implying neither denial nor approval, and offers a personal loan officer review.
"So you won't need to repeat yourself" is slightly optimistic, since the loan officer will likely re-verify figures, but the callback notes do capture everything shared.

judge.overall_notes: This was a sensitive negative-equity lead, handled with empathy, no rate or approval implications, and no hint of denial. All details were collected and a callback was booked with a clear time.
